role: Peripheral clock gating, peripheral reset, and CPU clock-source select. Pure data: every field here is plain RMW storage with no polled ready-bit and no side effect other than gating a clock or reset line. esp-soc's chip file (chips/esp32c3.json) currently lists SYSTEM as "model": "stub" -- this file promotes it to a real regmap.
verified: 2026-08-24 every offset, bit position and reset value below is quoted from the cited header at the pinned tag; the C3 TRM PDF was not consulted. Cross-checked behaviourally against components/esp_hw_support/port/esp32c3/rtc_clk.c and rtc_clk_init.c (tag v6.0.2): the C3 clock-switch path (rtc_clk_cpu_freq_set_config, rtc_clk_bbpll_enable/configure) never polls any SYSTEM register for readiness -- BBPLL config goes through the analog REGI2C bus (regi2c_ctrl_ll_bbpll_calibration_start(), write-only from the CPU's point of view) and RTC-domain clock switches use fixed esp_rom_delay_us() waits, not status-bit polls. So unlike STM32's RCC, no field in this register file is a wait-for-set/wait-for-match target; a plain reads-as-written default cannot create a false boot spin here.

fields.name: CPUPERIOD_SEL
fields.why: rtc_clk_cpu_freq_to_pll_mhz()/clk_ll_cpu_set_freq_mhz_from_pll() write this to select the CPU divide ratio off the 480MHz/320MHz BBPLL tap once PLL is running; esp_rom_set_cpu_ticks_per_us() is told the resulting frequency directly by software, so this field does not itself need to be read back correctly for boot to proceed -- only stored so later reads (e.g. esp_clk_cpu_freq()) are self-consistent

fields.name: CPU_WAIT_MODE_FORCE_ON
fields.why: Keeps the CPU's AHB/APB clock alive during WFI so debuggers and the interrupt matrix keep working; reset default 1, plain storage

registers.name: SYSTEM_PERIP_CLK_EN0_REG
registers.reset: 0xFFFFFFFF (chip-default; individual field resets below, several default 0)

fields.name: TIMERGROUP_CLK_EN
fields.why: Gates TIMG0's APB clock. TIMG0 is used for the boot-time RTC calibration loop (TIMG_RTCCALICFG, see peripherals/esp32c3/timg-contract.json) and by esp_timer; the __attribute__((constructor)) enable_timer_group0_for_calibration() in rtc_time.c calls timg_ll_enable_bus_clock(0,true), which sets this bit before any calibration register is touched -- if this field is not modelled as real storage (reads back what was written) that ctor's own enable becomes unverifiable and a strict caller could legitimately check it first

fields.name: UART1_CLK_EN
fields.why: UART1 clock gate, not on the minimum console path (see UART0 below); included for completeness of this register

fields.name: WDG_CLK_EN
fields.why: Despite the name this does not gate the RTC watchdog (that lives entirely inside RTC_CNTL, always clocked from the RTC domain) -- 'WDG' here is the APB register-access clock for the RTC_CNTL block's APB-side shadow registers. Left as plain rw; no driver polls it

fields.name: UART_CLK_EN
fields.why: Gates UART0's APB clock -- the console. periph_module_enable(PERIPH_UART0_MODULE) sets this before uart_hal_init() touches any UART0 register; a UART0 access with this bit clear is undefined on real silicon, but ESP-IDF always sets it first on the boot path, so for a first blink+console slice this can default reset=1 and be treated as always-on without breaking anything observable

fields.name: TIMERS_CLK_EN
fields.why: Gates the two general-purpose 54-bit hardware timers inside TIMG (distinct from the calibration unit and from MWDT); not on the blink/console path

registers.note: Register also carries SPI2/SPI3/SPI4/I2C/I2S/PWM/RMT/LEDC/PCNT/TWAI/UHCI/ADC/SYSTIMER/USB_DEVICE gate bits (system_reg.h:76-263) -- all plain rw, omitted here as not on the minimum boot+blink+console path. No GPIO clock-gate bit exists in this register or in PERIP_CLK_EN1: the GPIO matrix has no software clock gate on ESP32-C3, unlike STM32's IOPENR/AHBENR. That is a real difference from the STM32 checklist in docs/architectures.md 3.3 item 5 worth calling out explicitly so nobody goes looking for one.

fields.name: TIMERGROUP_RST
fields.why: timg_ll_reset_register(0), called by the same constructor as TIMERGROUP_CLK_EN above, pulses this bit; mirrors the enable register bit-for-bit, plain storage

fields.name: WDG_RST
fields.why: APB-side reset for RTC_CNTL's bus interface, not the watchdog itself; see WDG_CLK_EN above

fields.name: UART_RST
fields.why: UART0 peripheral reset line; periph_module_reset(PERIPH_UART0_MODULE) pulses it before init

fields.name: SOC_CLK_SEL
fields.why: Selects the SoC root clock source (XTAL / PLL / RC_FAST) for the AHB/APB fabric, distinct from CPU_PER_CONF which only picks the CPU's own divide ratio off that root. Written by rtc_clk_cpu_freq_set_config() via clk_ll_cpu_set_src(); read back nowhere in a spin -- rtc_clk_cpu_freq_get_config() (used for diagnostics, not boot gating) reads it back, so storage alone is sufficient

fields.name: PRE_DIV_CNT
fields.why: APB pre-divider off the selected SOC_CLK_SEL source; plain storage, no poll

not_covered: SYSTEM_CPU_INTR_FROM_CPU_0..3_REG (software-triggered interrupt lines, offsets 0x028-0x034) are plain rw storage too but belong with the interrupt-matrix work (esp-soc's chips/esp32c3.json INTMATRIX entry), not this clock/reset file.
